decision: runtime-keyed warm QueryRuntime caching (PRs #528-531) clears the p95/RSS/recall gate
method: scripts/m2_warm_runtime_benchmark.py run twice per fixture as separate subprocess invocations (baseline: runtime=None, exact pre-M2 code path per QueryRuntime's own byte-equivalence tests; runtime: one shared QueryRuntime across all repeated calls), each priming the on-disk index once (excluded from timing) then issuing every task question repeatedly, reporting p50/p95/p99 wall-clock latency across all repeated calls, this process's peak RSS (resource.getrusage), and recall/required-file-recall against self-repo benchmarks/tasks/archex_*.yaml expected_files (medium fixture only -- the large external fixture has no labeled expected_files).

medium.note: p95 improvement measured at 24.9% (5 repeats/task), 24.6% (10 repeats/task), and 25.5% (15 repeats/task, the recorded run) across three separate measurements -- right at the 25% target with meaningful run-to-run noise at this fixture's scale (186 files); clears the bar at the higher sample count but is not comfortably clear of it. The large fixture below shows the same effect far more decisively, consistent with caching benefit scaling with the BM25/graph reconstruction cost a bigger repo imposes on every cold warm-path rebuild.

large.repo: django/django (shallow clone, HEAD at benchmark time)
large.note: No labeled expected_files for this external fixture; recall is not scored here -- byte-equivalence is established by the medium fixture and by PR #529's own unit/integration tests.
